significance: A gurdwara in the Babey Beri locality of Sialkot marking a place where Guru Nanak is remembered to have stayed, built by Natha Singh and photographed as early as about 1910. Damaged in the unrest around the Babri Masjid dispute, it was restored in the 2010s and reopened to Sikh pilgrims from India in November 2012.
story: Guru Nanak is said to have rested here under a beri (jujube) tree, still standing, and to have met Hamza Ghaus, a Sufi saint of Sialkot.
